claims.text: The as-processed HfNbTiVAl10 alloy has a hierarchical heterostructure.
The hierarchical heterostructure comprises multiscale grain-boundary features and phase distributions.
A CNN can extract structural descriptors representing the hierarchical heterostructure from high-resolution images.
A downstream predictive model can use the extracted descriptors to estimate Young's modulus.
A downstream predictive model can use the extracted descriptors to estimate yield strength.
A downstream predictive model can use the extracted descriptors to estimate fracture-related behavior.
Grain-size distribution mediates the relationship between the hierarchical heterostructure and macroscopic mechanical properties.
Phase-boundary complexity mediates the relationship between the hierarchical heterostructure and macroscopic mechanical properties.
Defect density mediates the relationship between the hierarchical heterostructure and macroscopic mechanical properties.
The machine-learning model can learn nonlinear mappings between microstructural descriptors and mechanical responses.
These learned mappings can capture the effect of hierarchical heterogeneity on mechanical performance without finite-element simulation.
The ML approach will make predictions approximately ten times faster than conventional simulations.
The ML approach will improve predictive accuracy by more than 10% relative to conventional simulations.
Conventional finite-element and continuum simulations are currently used to predict tensile and fracture properties of HfNbTiVAl10.
Predictive performance may fail when test-sample microstructures lie outside the training-data distribution.
Extreme operating conditions such as very high strain rates may place samples outside the model's applicable domain.
The degree of improvement in accuracy and speed depends on the quality, diversity, and representativeness of the training data.
Microstructural nuances omitted from training data may reduce predictive performance.
Independent tensile and fracture measurements can be used to compare errors from the ML model and conventional finite-element simulations.
The hypothesis is declared falsified only if the ML method both fails to improve predictive accuracy by at least 10% and fails to reduce computation time by roughly an order of magnitude.

contradictions.description: The principal target is broadly described as 'fracture behavior' or 'fracture-related behavior,' whereas the falsification experiment operationalizes it only as fracture toughness; these are not necessarily interchangeable.
